comparisons.peer_summary: Net credit losses increased 40% to $9.0 billion, with consumer net credit losses rising 39% to $8.6 billion and corporate net credit losses increasing to $397 million from $250 million.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and Citigroup reported significant increases in credit loss metrics in 2024, with credit cards being a common driver. BAC reported a $1.4 billion increase in its Provision for Credit Losses to $5.8 billion, primarily driven by credit card loan growth and asset quality deterioration. Citigroup reported a 40% increase in Net Credit Losses to $9.0 billion, with consumer net credit losses (largely driven by Branded Cards and Retail Services) rising 39% to $8.6 billion. Both disclosures highlight the pressure on credit card portfolios in 2024, though BAC reports the income statement provision while C reports the resulting net credit losses.

comparisons.comparison: While both companies disclose their 2024 Provision for Credit Losses, the trends and drivers differ significantly. Bank of America saw an increase of $1.4 billion, driven largely by credit card growth and commercial real estate office deterioration. In contrast, JPMorgan's provision decreased to $762 million from $2.1 billion in the prior year. JPM's 2024 provision was driven by net charge-offs in Real Estate/Office and downgrades in Real Estate, but the overall provision was lower than BAC's, reflecting different scales and portfolio compositions, particularly the significant allowance additions for First Republic in JPM's prior year.
